scope.title: Preparation and preservation
scope.boundary: Local release projections, preservation and honest readiness through the real preparation function and CLI. Field-level parser variations stay in executable tests.

initial_state: Previous-version package and README; current profile; release-notes human prefix/suffix around a stale generated region; an immutable earlier release.yaml; existing release index and copied adapter manifest. Current release.yaml, standing record, npm publication report and timing document are absent.
Run ordinary prepare_release(v0.3.5) once; establish validate_pending_release_artifacts returns [] before a negative case mutation. Capture literal facts independently for REL-TC-001.
Write packages/rigorloop/dist/metadata/adapter-artifacts-v0.3.5.json containing {} followed by a newline.
In release.yaml, set manifest_version from the independently read fixture adapter manifest; replace pending results/required gate fields with pass. Keep smoke tool versions and evidence nonempty.
In the adapter report, set source_commit to 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567, date to 2026-08-06, each pending sha256 to 64 a characters and pending results to pass.
Run normal and approval-driven preparation as in the reference test, capture the resulting complete tree, and require check=True succeeds before applying a negative variant.
fixtures.limitation: Synthetic finalized local evidence tests format/preservation only; it is not actual qualification, smoke or publication evidence.

cases.title: Prepare correct release projections without manufacturing observed results
cases.risk: Preparation silently changes unrelated content, projects the wrong version, or generates a false qualification/publication pass.

conditions: Use unprepared with independent target version 0.3.5 and the ten expected changed paths. Set package name to @example/previous-name; add x-test-preserved={"enabled":true,"values":[1,2]}. Snapshot the parsed package object.
Exercise ordinary and approval-driven preparation separately. For approval-driven input, pre-create the standing record with Version decision: patch and Change summary: Reviewed compatibility repair.
Approval-driven timing starts absent or contains exactly # existing diagnostic evidence\ncreated_at: pending\n. This deliberately incomplete document tests preservation, not format acceptance.

when: Prepare v0.3.5 through the real planner and writes, then inspect actual file paths, content and generated pending facts.
then: Package name is @xiongxianfei/rigorloop and version is 0.3.5; README names 0.3.5 and latest, and the complete supplied version-decision text survives. Removing only name/version from both parsed package objects leaves equal remaining keys and values; formatting is outside this assertion.

For ordinary preparation, the actual created/modified path set equals the ten independently declared expected_changed_paths, with no deletions or unreported writes. Approval-driven mode neither creates nor modifies timing.yaml and omits it from changed_paths.

npm-publication.md retains Status: pending-publication and published: false; codex/claude smoke results remain pending-publication. Approval-driven evidence contains no generated pass assertion or invented duration.

gaps: Write the profile package version: The existing test checks changed paths and repeatability but never reads the resulting package version.
Set profile-owned identity and preserve unrelated package metadata: No existing preparation test observes package-field preservation or profile-name replacement.
Generate exactly the selected local preparation surfaces: The existing test checks the reported changed_paths but does not compare them with the actual first-call filesystem diff.
Generated pending evidence has a valid pending shape: The existing test checks only errors == []; assert the pending values independently so producer and validator cannot agree on fabricated success.
Approval-driven preparation does not invent timing measurements: The approval-driven branch explicitly skips new timing output, but no preparation test asserts absence.
Approval-driven preparation preserves existing timing bytes: The branch preserves existing timing files, but no preparation test observes that behavior.

cases.title: Repeated preparation preserves a coherent prepared or finalized tree
cases.risk: Repeated generation changes files or reports changes despite identical inputs.

conditions: Prepare an ordinary tree and separately use the finalized-local fixture with successfully checked complete evidence. Snapshot complete relative path/byte maps.

when: Repeat preparation with unchanged inputs for each tree.
then: The complete tree remains byte-identical and changed_paths is empty; finalized evidence is not reset to pending.

cases.title: Preparation preserves human narrative and immutable earlier evidence
cases.risk: Replacing a generated region consumes nearby human text or rewrites an earlier release file.

conditions: Place exact human prefix/suffix bytes, including a literal pass example, around generated regions. Snapshot earlier release evidence.

when: Prepare the new release using real file writes.
then: Human bytes and their positions outside generated regions remain unchanged; earlier release evidence is byte-identical.
A human pass example does not become generated proof or select a different planning branch.

gaps: Preserve human narrative and earlier release evidence: Existing narrative assertions check substring presence; compare exact outside-region bytes and their positions.

cases.title: Check mode reports readiness without changing files through function or CLI
cases.risk: A diagnostic check writes files or accepts an unprepared tree.

conditions: Use one unprepared and one successfully prepared tree; snapshot every relative path and byte sequence before each check.

when: Invoke prepare_release with check=True and the actual prepare-release CLI --check on each tree.
then: Unprepared input rejects with the planned updates and unsuccessful CLI status; prepared input reports no changes and CLI success.
Both success and rejection preserve the complete tree. Check success establishes local preparation only.

gaps: The public CLI check reports a prepared no-op: The existing CLI case checks status and output, but needs an independent before/after tree comparison.
The public CLI check rejects an unprepared tree without writes: The existing rejection case calls the function only; add an actual CLI invocation to observe exit and dispatch.

cases.title: Pending evidence is complete, unambiguous and cannot claim publication
cases.risk: Structurally plausible generated evidence hides missing proof or claims an unobserved publication.

conditions: Use a successfully validated prepared tree. Independently remove a required section/row/target, duplicate a row, insert an unknown result, claim publication or disagree between readable and structured smoke facts.

when: Validate pending artifacts after each single mutation; keep all unrelated facts valid.
then: The valid pending tree passes without any implied public result.
Missing standing record, adapter/recovery sections, required preflight/registry rows or selected-target smoke rejects; duplicate, extra-target and unknown-result rows reject.
A published claim in pending evidence, wrong command serialization or disagreement between text and structured facts rejects with the responsible field identified.

cases.title: Invalid finalized-looking evidence is scheduled for correction
cases.risk: A pass token makes the planner preserve malformed evidence, or an unrelated fixture defect causes a misleading rejection.

conditions: For each variant, establish that check mode succeeds before the defining mutation; capture the mutated tree before the failing check.

then: Raise ReleaseProfileError with prepare-release would update and docs/releases/v0.3.5/release.yaml.
The mutated tree remains byte-for-byte unchanged by check mode.

gaps: Invalid finalized-looking evidence is scheduled for correction: Existing negative fixtures do not prove a successful finalized baseline before mutation; several hardcode manifest v0.1.5. Start from finalized-local, isolate the fault and compare bytes after the check.

parameters.mutation: Remove adapter_paths, preserving the following instruction_entrypoints section.
Set the codex passing smoke evidence field to an empty string.
Set the first passing smoke tool_version to three spaces.
Set the first passing smoke evidence field to three spaces.

cases.title: Local preparation makes no external operation
cases.risk: The result reports no external actions even though preparation performs a process or network call.

conditions: Use the real planner and filesystem writes. Install fail-on-call spies at subprocess.run, subprocess.Popen, urllib.request.urlopen and socket.create_connection for the duration of the call. Record each attempted call before failing.

then: Preparation succeeds, result.external_actions == (), and every spy call log is empty.
No Git tag, push, GitHub release operation or npm lookup/publish is invoked through those boundaries.

gaps: Local preparation makes no external operation: The existing test asserts only the returned external_actions tuple. Observe external call boundaries; a self-reported empty tuple is insufficient. This boundary list must track any newly introduced process/network client.

cases.title: Rerun repairs a partial local write without claiming readiness
cases.risk: An interrupted preparation leaves mixed versions that are later mistaken for a complete release.

conditions: Prepare a separate fresh control tree normally and capture its expected completed file set.

In the case tree, intercept Path.write_text only for docs/releases/v0.3.5/release.yaml and raise OSError("injected preparation write failure") before writing that file. Delegate every other write to the real filesystem.

when: After the raised error, remove the fault and inspect the partial tree before retry.
then: The first call raises the injected OSError; it does not return a success result.
At interruption, package.json has version 0.3.5 while release.yaml is absent; rollback of earlier writes is not assumed.
Validation of the partial tree returns a missing pending release artifact diagnostic naming release.yaml.
The retry produces the same relative paths and bytes as the normal control tree; independently assert package version 0.3.5 and pending publication facts as in REL-TC-001.
Final check mode reports no changed_paths. No public release readiness or executed-check pass is inferred from successful local preparation.

gaps: Rerun repairs a partial local write without claiming readiness: Add the exact write-boundary injection and recovery assertions; no existing preparation method exercises this interruption.

cases.title: Malformed generated regions stop preparation before writes
cases.risk: Malformed region matching overwrites human content or generates a partially trusted release.

conditions: Start from a valid generated region; independently remove its end marker, nest another region, mismatch namespace/surface or introduce an unknown surface. Snapshot all files after mutation.

when: Run real preparation for each malformed-region variant.
then: Reject the defining marker defect before any file mutation; retain the complete malformed input for diagnosis.

gaps: A missing generated-region end marker stops before writes: The source explicitly rejects this malformed region, but the preparation module has no corresponding boundary test.

Generated regions reject nesting mismatched namespace and unknown surfaces: No linked Release method establishes nesting or unknown-surface rejection. The inspected replacement helper searches only a known start prefix and matching end; implement and test the contract at preparation before relying on this protection.
